transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 63 minutes
Attendees: Jared Liu (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (CTO, Aureus), Liam O'Connell (ML Eng), Ruchi Patel (SRE)

Summary:
Quick lab-style deep dive covering hybrid routing strategies, RoPE scaling impacts on long-context decoding, MoE routing costs for Qwen/Mistral/Llama families, and practical KV prewarm/batching trade-offs for VPC/on-prem deployments. Actionable bench plan and immediate config deliverables agreed.

Topics:
- RoPE ratio (decay vs rescale) sensitivity across Mistral/Qwen/Llama
- MoE gating costs and token affinity vs generalist routing
- KV prewarm / shard strategies for low tail latency
- Quantization knobs (q4_0, q5, int8 vs q8_0) and perf regressions
- VPC network egress and on-prem NIC tuning

Action items (summary): see action_items field for owners/due dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jared Liu: okay everyone thanks for hopping on, uh today is 63 minutes on my calendar, right? we've got a fairly packed lab, so Priya's going to drive the perf side and i'll do a little framing. Maya, thanks for organizing on your side.
[00:12] Maya Thompson: yeah thanks Jared, we pushed this up because we hit some weird tail spikes during batch inference overnight — some requests at 99.9 were 1.4s while the 95th is 0.25 so it's really the tail, and we suspect it's to do with routing and kv cache misses.
[00:26] Priya Nair: ok got it, that's the classic warm vs cold kv problem, and given you have a mix of short search style prompts and long-context generative flows, we'll look at rope scaling and also gating behavior on MoE. do you have a quick profile of token lengths?
[00:38] Liam O'Connell: yeah i'll share — most are sub-512 but we've got a 7% tail beyond 4k because of multi-document summarization. thats where RoPE differences show up i think.
[00:50] Ruchi Patel: and we're running in a VPC with private dedicated nodes — so there's some NAT and cross-subnet routing, not totally flat L2, and we do use KMS for key wrap.
[01:02] Priya Nair: perfect that's helpful. quick agenda: 1) verify cost model for hybrid routing (route-by-latency vs route-by-cost), 2) run targeted bench plan Priya -> show scripts, 3) talk RoPE scaling experiments and what to expect across Llama/Mistral/Qwen, 4) kv prewarm and microbatch config.
[01:20] Jared Liu: and call out that for MoE models we often see the per-token gating overhead and remote expert transfer costs dominate when sequence lengths go up, so routing economics change.
[01:30] Maya Thompson: when you say gating overhead what is the magnitude? we counted 8-12% CPU + extra network in our in-house runs.
[01:38] Priya Nair: depends — lightweight gating (top-1) can add like 5-10ms per token on CPU-bound softmax gating in Python stacks, but on Redwood runtime with optimized kernels it's more like 1-3ms; however, if experts are remote and you need serialization + RPC it's additive. so for short bursts gating overhead percentage can kill throughput.
[01:55] Liam O'Connell: do you recommend moving to token-affinity routing to keep tokens on the same device? we tried sticky routing but saw imbalance.
[02:04] Priya Nair: sticky/token-affinity is good when your workload has locality — e.g., streaming chat where the same conversation stays on a single shard. For multi-user batched workload, affinity causes skew. Hybrid routing that prefers affinity for sessions older than N tokens and otherwise routes by cost works well. that's what we call session-aware hybrid.
[02:22] Ruchi Patel: any pointer on how to tune N?
[02:26] Priya Nair: tune by measuring sequence turn length distribution. pick N at the 50-75th percentile of session lengths so you get benefit for most long runs without causing imbalance. we'll include a script.
[02:36] Jared Liu: ok moving to RoPE: we ran into Llama showing drift with long contexts vs Mistral which seems to tolerate larger rescale factors. Priya can you walk the attendees through what we changed and why?
[02:47] Priya Nair: sure. quick primer for folks: RoPE (rotary positional embeddings) implementations differ — some models apply decay on higher frequencies (RoPE decay) and others rescale. empirically, rescaling factors that compress high-frequency content reduce drift for very long contexts but can hurt near-term alignment for short prompts. we did experiments with "rope_ratio" hyperparam — we use 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.2 as sweeps.
[03:12] Liam O'Connell: that's interesting — do these changes require re-tokenization or can we just change runtime multiply?
[03:18] Priya Nair: runtime-only changes for many ops — it's a multiply inside the rotary projection before attention. so very low-cost to test. caveat: some model weights were trained with a particular rope scaling, so large deltas can create scoring shifts. hence do a small sweep first.
[03:32] Maya Thompson: what did you see for Mistral vs Qwen vs Llama? any clear winners?
[03:37] Priya Nair: for our benchmarks: Mistral-7B tolerated rescale up to 1.2 with minimal downstream quality regressions on summarization prompts; Llama-2-Chat showed more regression at 1.1+, Qwen-7 had mixed signals — it benefited on hallucination reduction with 0.9 but decoding entropy changed. we'll share the quality vs latency plotted curves.
[03:58] Jared Liu: and important note — RoPE tuning can change KV cache hit behavior because the keys differ, so you might see a transient drop in cache hit rate after rolling a config. expect an initial noise window.
[04:10] Ruchi Patel: ah that might explain our overnight spikes, we did a model swap last week.
[04:15] Priya Nair: exactly. follow a canary rollout pattern — small traffic slice, validate reranking prompts and long-form test set. Redwood Console can automate rollback on quality regressions.
[04:25] Jared Liu: next topic: microbatching and KV prewarm. Priya?
[04:29] Priya Nair: yes. key knobs: microbatch size, microbatch interval, and KV prewarm policy. For low-latency SLOs, keep microbatching small (1-8) and enable prefix K/V caching aggressively for repeating sessions. In your VPC setup you should prefer in-node KV cache (shard per GPU) rather than cross-node fetch. That reduces tail by 2x in our labs.
[04:50] Liam O'Connell: but we only have 2 GPUs per host, so sharding gets tricky with large KV for 4k contexts.
[04:57] Priya Nair: two options: 1) increase KV quant footprint (store compressed kv in q4_0) to fit in GPU memory, 2) use shard+prefetch where hot keys stay on-device and cold keys are fetched async. For your prompt distribution: 70% <512 so hot keys cover most. We'll show how to set the hot-key threshold in the runtime.
[05:16] Maya Thompson: about quant: we tested q4_0 and saw a small perf jump but some quality dip for multi-doc summarization. Thoughts?
[05:25] Priya Nair: q4_0 gives nice memory savings and faster matmul, but q4 variants sometimes produce higher logits noise for nuanced generations. q5 or int8 on critical layers (FFN) is a good tradeoff — we recommend layerwise quant profile: q4_0 for attention weights, q5 for FFN, keep embedding and norm in fp16. that usually preserves quality while giving 30-45% token-cost reduction.
[05:46] Ruchi Patel: do you have prebuilt quant profiles for Mistral/Qwen/Llama?
[05:50] Priya Nair: yes — Redwood Optimize ships model-specific defaults. we'll attach the profiles in S3 link in the follow-up. also note that per-model sensitivity varies: Llama tends to be more sensitive in FFN layers, Mistral tolerates more aggressive attention quant.
[06:03] Jared Liu: switching to MoE economics: when you have sparse routing you save FLOPs but incur routing overhead and potential network transfer for remote experts. We recommend hybrid: use MoE for background batch-heavy tasks (reranking, embedding-expansion) and use dense variants for low-latency tail-critical paths.
[06:20] Liam O'Connell: can you quantify the breakpoint where MoE becomes cheaper?
[06:24] Priya Nair: rough rule: if average sequence length > 1024 and per-request token count per second is high (sustained throughput > 200 tokens/sec per user), MoE can be cost-effective. But if you need 99.9 latency below 300ms, the extra jitter from remote experts often breaks SLAs. We'll provide a cost calculator spreadsheet.
[06:44] Maya Thompson: we have a pricing constraint — our infra budget wants to max at $0.0009/token for generative. any guidance?
[06:51] Jared Liu: that's tight. two levers: aggressive batching with prefix cache for the 70% short ones, and route the long ones to cheaper quantized Mistral or Qwen with lower throughput cost. use fallback policies for capacity bursts.
[07:02] Priya Nair: also consider model multiplexing — keep a smaller dense Llama instance for short completions and a quantized MoE for heavy summaries but cap usage with token budgets via routing. Redwood routing rules can enforce per-tenant token-slices.
[07:14] Ruchi Patel: network-wise, any VPC tuning notes? we saw a few hundred microsecond increase due to MTU mismatches across subnets.
[07:21] Priya Nair: yep check MTU and jumbo frames; also ensure your NIC offload (RSS/GRO/LRO) is enabled on the RDMA fabric if using on-prem. For cloud, pick placement groups/elastic fabric options. And reduce cross-az chatty RPCs by co-locating frequently called experts.
[07:36] Liam O'Connell: can Redwood runtime prefer local experts?
[07:39] Priya Nair: yes, the runtime has a locality-aware scheduler. you can set a locality threshold — prefer local experts unless local load > 80% then spill to remote. That threshold is tunable.
[07:49] Jared Liu: let's demo a quick bench — Priya has a script that simulates 70/30 short/long and toggles rope_ratio and routing policy. Priya do you want to share terminal?
[07:56] Priya Nair: i'm going to paste results from an internal run (lightly redacted). note these are local lab numbers but comparable.
[08:04] Priya Nair (screen): run id: mr-1223, workload: mix A (70% <512, 23% 512-2k, 7% >2k)
[08:12] Priya Nair (screen): baseline (Llama dense fp16): p95=260ms, p99=760ms, cost/token=0.0012
[08:20] Priya Nair (screen): Mistral q4_0 + rope_ratio=1.05, prefix-KV-hot: p95=210ms, p99=430ms, cost/token=0.00078
[08:34] Priya Nair (screen): MoE (Qwen-sparse) top1 gating local-expert bias: p95=190ms, p99=950ms (high tail due to remote expert fetch), cost/token=0.00055
[08:47] Maya Thompson: wow that p99 for MoE is bad in raw numbers.
[08:50] Priya Nair: yes unless you can guarantee locality or prewarm the experts. we saw that pre-warming the top hot keys for Qwen-sparse reduced p99 to 520ms and cost increased slightly due to memory footprint. there's a cost/latency balance.
[09:05] Liam O'Connell: what's the prewarm strategy? just sequentially prime popular conversation keys?
[09:10] Priya Nair: two things — proactive prewarm where you identify top-n tokens or sessions and prefetch their KV to the expert GPU; and adaptive prefetch where you watch first N tokens and asynchronously fetch likely experts. Redwood runtime supports both.
[09:22] Ruchi Patel: will prewarm increase memory pressure? for us yes, our GPU RAM is tight.
[09:26] Priya Nair: yes it's a trade. you can prewarm only embeddings and recent kv slices; compress with q4_0 for storage. also set a TTL for prewarm so you evict stale ones.
[09:36] Jared Liu: let's talk about Canary/rollout: we recommend 5-10% traffic slice with A/B compare on metrics: p95, p99, perplexity delta and business KPI. Redwood Console can do rolling canary with auto-fallback if p99 exceeds threshold or quality regressions found.
[09:52] Maya Thompson: back to rope tuning lifecycle — do you recommend model retrain after rope change?
[09:57] Priya Nair: if you adjust rope_ratio slightly (<=10%), usually runtime-only is okay. If you need larger changes due to long-context improvements, retraining or fine-tuning is safer. Also can do light fine-tune with LoRA on positional encodings.
[10:08] Liam O'Connell: one of our devs asked about KV shard failures — we saw occasional OOM on a shard and it caused large fallback to remote which spiked p99. any guardrails?
[10:18] Priya Nair: runtime-level guardrails: soft-limit per-shard memory alarm that triggers shedding or temporary throttling, and you can set a spill-to-disk or async prefetch path that trades latency for stability. Redwood's recommended config is 90% soft cap, 95% throttle, and 99% hard OOM with auto-restart.
[10:36] Ruchi Patel: how do we test these in our VPC without touching prod?
[10:40] Jared Liu: set up a staging VPC with identical topology and run the bench scripts. Redwood can spin a short-lived dedicated fleet in your VPC for the tests; that avoids touching prod and mirrors latency. we'll arrange that.
[10:50] Maya Thompson: one more question on security — when you do KV prewarm is any PII in the kv cache? we need guidance for KMS/HSM.
[10:58] Priya Nair: good callout. Treat KV as sensitive if context contains PII. Redwood supports encrypting KV in transit and at rest with customer-managed KMS keys. For on-prem, you can use HSM-backed key wrapping. Also we recommend redaction rules before caching if PII is present.
[11:12] Liam O'Connell: any pitfalls for quant + rope change interacting?
[11:16] Priya Nair: yes — quant noise can amplify positional embedding shifts. if you change rope and quantize at the same time it's harder to attribute quality drift. do sequential: 1) roll rope change canary, 2) verify quality, 3) then apply quant profile canary.
[11:30] Jared Liu: ok we've got about 12 minutes left — let's outline bench plan and who does what. Priya, can you summarize the exact steps we'll run in the lab?
[11:39] Priya Nair: yep. Step 1: ingest Aureus prompt trace (anonymized) into perf harness — Liam to provide. Step 2: baseline run on dense Llama fp16. Step 3: Mistral q4_0 runs with rope_ratio sweep [0.9, 1.0, 1.05, 1.1]. Step 4: Qwen-sparse top1 with and without local-expert prewarm. Step 5: collect p50/p95/p99, cost/token, cache hit rate, and quality scores (ROUGE/BLEU/Perplexity). Step 6: Redwood shares CSV + plots, then we meet next week for decision.
[11:59] Maya Thompson: timeline sounds good. can Redwood also run a short on-prem NIC tuning checklist?
[12:04] Jared Liu: yes i'll attach a one-pager. we'll also include the S3 link to quant profiles, perf scripts, and the console canary template.
[12:14] Ruchi Patel: thanks — also if we enable locality bias what's the mechanism to detect imbalance and auto-adjust?
[12:19] Priya Nair: the runtime emits a per-expert heatmap and imbalance score. you can set an auto-throttle policy: if imbalance > 1.5x for > 30s reduce affinity threshold. We'll include recommended thresholds.
[12:31] Liam O'Connell: last quick thing: is there any recommeded guard for token-length explosion from adversarial prompts? we had a user that sent 200k token doc once.
[12:39] Priya Nair: set hard token caps at the gateway and streaming cutoffs. Redwood supports per-route token limits and backpressure. Also enable prefiltering to chunk or reject very long requests.
[12:50] Jared Liu: great. quick recap of next steps then we can close.
[12:55] Maya Thompson: thanks all, this was super helpful.
[13:00] Jared Liu: thanks team, we'll share the bench artifacts and reconvene on 2026-12-21.

End of transcript.
